units.title: What Are My Goals?
units.intro: What do **you** want to reach? This unit helps you think about your **goals** and the **people** who can help you.

pins.text: Parents or grandparents?
A teacher?
Friends?
Others? Who do you think?

lessons.title: Who can help me meet my goals?

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: This unit is about **goals**.
You will think about **skills** that help you **reach** your goals.

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What is a **goal**?
What are **your** goals?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Goals for different times
body: The book asks about goals for **three** times. Move the slider.

states.label: This semester
states.text: What goal do you want to reach **this semester**?

states.label: This year
states.text: What goal do you want to reach **this year**?

states.label: The future
states.text: What goal do you want to reach **in the future**?

cards.title: Activity II: think and talk
body: Is it **easy** to reach your goals? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Who can help me?
body: The book asks: **who** can help you meet your goals?
Tap the people. The book does not say who. You decide!

cards.title: Remember
body: A goal can be for **this semester**, **this year** or **the future**.
Other people can **help** us meet our goals.

cards.title: Memory trick: S-Y-F
body: "**S**mall **Y**oung **F**eet" climb the goal ladder.

cards.q: For which times does Activity II ask about goals?

cards.title: A person I admire
body: To **admire** someone means to think they are very good.
Write the name of a person you admire. List the **qualities** that make him or her admirable.

cards.title: Activity II: think and talk
body: **Why** do we admire people?
Which qualities would **you** like to have? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Words for good qualities
body: Here are some words you can use: **kind**, **honest**, **hard-working**, **brave**, **helpful**.
*These words are our own examples; the book gives no list.*

Learn good qualities from people you admire.

units.title: Friendship Formation
units.intro: How do we choose **good friends**? What are friends for, and how much should we do for them?

scenarios.title: How much shall I do for a friend?

pins.text: 1. My friend wants me to miss a class. What would I do?
2. My friend wants me to always take my side in a conflict. What would I do?
3. My friend wants me to help steal money. What would I do?
4. My friend wants me to keep a crime secret. What would I do?
5. My friend wants me to copy my homework. What would I do?
6. My friend wants me to go against my values. What would I do?
7. My friend tells me he/she is HIV positive. What would I do?
8. My friend wants me to jump the school fence. What would I do?
9. My friend wants me to swim in a dam. What would I do?

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: This unit is about **friends**.
What makes a **good** friend? How do we **choose** friends?

cards.title: Activities I and II: think and talk
body: What is a **friend**?
What **criteria** (reasons) do you use to choose a friend?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity III: think and talk
body: Is it fair to choose friends by **culture, religion, ethnic origin** or **area**? Why?
Is it **easy** to choose a friend?
**Who** can help you choose friends?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: Which things does the book ask about choosing friends by?

cards.title: Agree, disagree or not sure?
body: The book gives **8 statements**. Tick **agree**, **disagree** or **not sure**.

cards.title: The 8 statements
head: No.
Statement
rows: Friends must be of the same religion.
One can have friendship with the opposite sex.
Friends are needed only in bad situations.
Friends must have the same interest.
One can get all he/she needs from friends.

cards.title: Talk about them
body: There is no answer key. Discuss each statement with your group and teacher.
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What can **you** do to **form** a friendship?
What can you do to **keep** (maintain) a friendship?
*The book gives no model answer.*

lessons.title: How much shall I do for a friend?

cards.title: How much shall I do for a friend?
body: The book gives **9 situations**. Tap each one. What would **you** do?

cards.title: Think before you say yes
body: Some things a friend asks may be **wrong** or **dangerous**: stealing money, jumping the school fence, swimming in a dam.
A good friend can also say **no**.

cards.title: A friend with HIV
body: Situation 7: "If my friend told me she/he was **HIV positive**, I would..."
Unit 5 talks more about HIV and about not being afraid.

cards.title: Activity II: think and talk
body: What things **would** you do for your close friends?
What things **wouldn't** you do?
*The book gives no model answer.*

steps.text: **Sara** and **Mussa** were classmates. They were **clever** and **helped each other** study. They went to school and the **library** together.
Sara's parents heard she was going out with Mussa. They **warned** her. Mussa's parents did the **same**.
Both sets of parents did all they could to **separate** them.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What would you do if you were Sara? Mussa? Their parents?
Why did the parents warn them?
Will Sara and Mussa **succeed** in their study? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Think and talk more
body: Is it hard for a boy and a girl to be friends? Why?
Is it common in your area for a boy and a girl to be **close friends**?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: How did Sara and Mussa help each other?

the reasons you use to choose
the way of life of a group
the ethnic group you come from
boys for girls, girls for boys

Sara and Mussa helped each other study.

units.title: Gender and Gender Roles
units.intro: Is some work only for **boys** or only for **girls**? Look at gender roles in your **family**, **school** and **community**.

pins.text: 1. Who is given more attention?
2. Who does the cooking?
3. Who looks after the animals?
4. Who is sent to school first?
5. Who washes the clothes?
6. Who fetches water?
7. Who fetches firewood?
8. Who rides a bicycle?
9. Who cleans the house?
10. Who milks the cows?

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: This unit is about **gender** and **gender roles**.
You will look for gender roles and **stereotypes** in your community.

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What is **gender**?
What are **gender roles**?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: In your family, who usually...?
body: The book gives **10 questions**. For each, tick **boy** or **girl**. Tap each box.

cards.title: Activity III: think and talk
body: Should there be **special work** for boys or for girls? Why?
How should parents treat their **sons** and **daughters**? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: Which is one of the family questions?

cards.title: School activities: boy, girl or both?
head: No.
Activity
rows: digging and watering the school garden
planting trees in the school compound

cards.title: Tick boy, girl or both
body: Which activities are **usually** done by boys, girls or **both** in your school?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity II: think and talk
body: What stops **girls** from doing activities usually done by boys?
What stops **boys** from doing activities usually done by girls?
How can we **break** gender-biased attitudes?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What are **boys** allowed and not allowed to do in your community?
What are **girls** allowed and not allowed to do?
*The book gives no model answer.*

steps.text: The teacher asks **Fatuma** why she was **sleeping** in class. She was **tired**.
After school she fetches **water two kilometres** away. She collects **firewood** and **washes** the family's clothes.
Her mother is away **selling peanuts**. So Fatuma **cooks and serves dinner** and **washes the dishes**. She has no time for homework.
Her **brothers** do not help. They say it is "**girl's work**".
Her family would let her **drop out** if her brothers do well. The teacher says many girls say this. It should be **discussed in the community**.

cards.title: Sharing the work
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Now
states.text: Fatuma does **all** the work and cannot study.

states.label: Better?
states.text: What if her brothers **helped**? What do you think?

cards.title: Think and talk
body: How do you see Fatuma's situation? Why?
Is it common in your community? What should be done?
*The book gives no model answer.*

options.A: her mother is away selling peanuts

items.why: They say it is girl's work.

items.text: The teacher says Fatuma's problem should be discussed in the community.

items.why: Most of the time she doesn't.

units.title: Sexual and Physical Abuse
units.intro: You have the right to be **safe**. Learn to say **No** loudly and clearly, and how to deal with **bullies**.

pins.text: She said "No!" loudly and clearly: "I said No! And I mean No."
She pushed him away with all her strength.
She said: "If you try to touch me again, I will scream."
She said "No!" loudly and clearly: "I said No! And I mean No."
She pushed him away with all her strength.
She said: "If you try to touch me again, I will scream."

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: This unit is about staying **safe** from **abuse**: touches or actions that **hurt** or scare you.
You will learn **skills** to avoid it.

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What is a **good** touch?
What is a **bad** touch?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Good touch or bad touch?
body: The book lists **7 touches**. You mark them **√** (good), **X** (bad) or **?** (not sure).
They go from **holding hands** to **touches on private parts of the body**.
Discuss them with your teacher.

cards.title: Our safety tip
body: If a touch makes you feel **bad, scared or confused**, say **No**, move away and **tell an adult you trust**.
*This tip is ours; the book does not say it.*

lessons.title: How to say "No" loudly and clearly

steps.text: **Nati** is 15. **Paulina** is 13. Nati helps her with her **assignment**.
Nati says it is time to "**prove our love**". Paulina says **No**.
On the way home Nati pulls her to a **quiet place** and **holds her tightly**. She says "**Stop it!**"
"**I said No! And I mean No.**" She **pushes** him away and says she will **scream**.

cards.title: What Paulina did
body: Tap each box to see how she said **No loudly and clearly**.

cards.title: Saying No
body: Say **No** in a **loud** and **clear** voice.
Mean it. Paulina did not give in, even though she liked Nati.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What would you do if you were Paulina?
Did Paulina act **assertively** (strongly and clearly)? Why?
What would happen if Paulina **agreed**?
What **advice** would you give Nati?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What are **bullies**? What do they do?
**Why** do they behave like that?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Geresin the bully
body: **Geresin** is in **grade 6**. He always **fights** to show his **strength**.
He **forces** children to give him **money**, or he beats them. Many children **fear** him.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: Why do you think Geresin acts like this?
How can his schoolmates **deal** with him?
What can be done to **correct** bullies?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What are the **laws** and **norms** (customs) of your society about growing up and relationships?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Agree or disagree?
body: The book gives **8 statements** about the rules of society. You mark **√** (agree) or **X** (disagree). Some examples:
"One who feels **strong** has the right to **threaten** others."
"Children should not always accept their **parents' orders**."
"Eritrean state law encourages **early marriage**."

cards.title: Talk about them
body: Discuss all 8 statements with your teacher.
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: How do you mark the 4.4 statements?

glossary.meaning: to put your hand on someone
a person who hurts or scares weaker people
to say you will hurt someone

tips.text: Say No loudly and clearly, like Paulina.
Tell an adult you trust (our tip).
Bullies want to scare you. Talk about how to deal with them.

units.title: HIV and AIDS
units.intro: Learn how **HIV** is spread and how it is **not** spread. Facts help us **stop fear** and be kind.

notspread.title: What health workers say (not from the book)

pins.text: Hugging, holding hands and playing together do not spread HIV.
Sharing clothes or combs does not spread HIV.
Sitting next to someone with HIV is safe.
Mosquito bites do not spread HIV.

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will learn how **HIV** is spread, and how it is **not** spread.
Knowing the facts helps us **reduce fear**.

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: What is the **difference** between HIV and AIDS?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: True or false?
body: The book gives **8 statements**. Tick **true** or **false**.

cards.title: The 8 statements (5.1)
head: No.
Statement
rows: People with AIDS die from opportunistic diseases.
Many people with HIV can look and feel healthy for years.
People can have HIV but may not know it.
A blood test is the only way to tell if someone has HIV.
HIV destroys the body's defence cells.

cards.title: Talk about them
body: The book gives no answers. Work them out with your teacher.
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity III: think and talk
body: What do people in your community say about HIV and AIDS?
Can people with HIV be **easily identified**? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: How does a person get **infected** with HIV?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: True, false or not sure? (5.2)
body: The book gives **7 statements**. Some examples:
"HIV is spread by using **unsterilized needles** or other sharp things."
"An HIV positive **mother** can infect her **baby**."
"HIV can be spread through **mosquito bite**."
"Traditional practices like **circumcision** can transmit HIV."

cards.title: Talk about them
body: Discuss all 7 with your teacher.
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity III: think and talk
body: Which **cultural practices** in your community may help HIV spread? Which may stop it?
What can **you** do to reduce the spread of HIV and AIDS?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Activity I: think and talk
body: How is HIV **not** transmitted?
*The book gives no model answer.*

steps.text: **Asmerom** is in grade 6. He lives with his **two sisters**. He and his friend **Samson** play, study and go to school together.
Samson hears a **rumour**: Asmerom's mother died of HIV and AIDS **five years ago**. Classmates say Asmerom **might** be HIV positive.
What would **you** do if you were Samson?

cards.title: What health workers say
body: *This card is not from the book.* Health workers teach these facts. They help us **not be afraid** of friends like Asmerom.
Tap each picture.

cards.title: PLWHA
body: **PLWHA** means **People Living With HIV and AIDS**.
The book asks: how can we **reduce the fear** towards them?

cards.title: Think and talk
body: If you were Samson, what would you do?
If you were a classmate, how would you feel?
How would you act if your **desk mate** had HIV? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

units.title: Me and My Community
units.intro: What can **you** do for your **family**, **school** and **community**? How can we care for people in **need**?

pins.text: My family: what does my family expect me to do?
My school: health-damaging factors and their solutions
My community: problems and possible solutions
My family: what does my family expect me to do?
My school: health-damaging factors and their solutions
My community: problems and possible solutions

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: This unit helps you build **healthy**, **responsible** and **cooperative** relationships.
You will think about your **family**, **school** and **community**.

cards.title: What can I do for...?
body: Tap each circle.

cards.title: My family: think and talk
body: What do you do for your **family**?
Role play: a **misbehaving** child, then a **well-behaved** child.
What does your family **expect** from you? Which do you not do? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: My school
body: Make a list of things that **damage health** at school, and their **solutions**.
Which solutions can **students** do? What should **your** part be?

cards.title: My school: think and talk
body: What new **rules** should the school make to **promote health**?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: My community: think and talk
body: What **problems** are there in your community?
Pick **three** big problems and write possible **solutions**.
What is **your** role? Who can **support** you?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Sympathy and empathy
body: Lesson 6.2 is about caring for four groups: the **disabled**, **orphans**, the **elderly** and **PLWHA**.

cards.title: The disabled
body: The book says: "**Let's not isolate the disabled!**" Move the slider.

states.label: Included
states.text: Include everyone in play and work.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: List different types of **disabilities**.
What is your role in helping the disabled? What support would **you** want?
Who is responsible for helping them? What should the school do?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Orphans: Rahma
body: **Rahma** is in **grade six**. Her parents died when she was young.
She lives with her **aunt**. Her aunt is **determined** to help her.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What problems could Rahma face?
What support could you give to people like Rahma?
Whose responsibility is it to help orphans?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: The elderly
body: **Ato Abraham** is **90** and his wife is **85**. They **live alone**.
Their neighbour **Ato Erimias** and his family **support** them.

cards.title: Role-play and talk
body: What problems do Ato Abraham and his wife face?
Who could help the elderly? What could **you** do?
What do you **gain** by helping the elderly?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: PLWHA: think and talk
body: List the support you would need if you were **HIV positive**.
Who should support PLWHA? What is your role?
*The book gives no model answer.*

steps.text: **Visit** the elderly, the disabled or orphans in your community.
Find out **what kind of help** they need.
Plan **strategies** to help them. The book's example: "**Visiting them**".

cards.title: Remember
body: Care for **family, school and community**.
Include the **disabled**. Support **orphans**, the **elderly** and **PLWHA**.
